items.title: What Is Data Poisoning? How Attackers Corrupt AI Models and Datasets
items.summary: Data poisoning manipulates training, fine-tuning, evaluation, or retrieval data so an AI system learns corrupted behavior or produces attacker-chosen outcomes. This guide explains the mechanism, trade-offs, evaluation, and controls that matter in practice.

Jan Petrš is a roboticist, architect, and entrepreneur working at the intersection of robotics and construction. He is currently the co-founder of Déploya Robotics , an EPFL spin-off developing deployable robotic systems for automated façade installation. Previously, he was a Postdoctoral Researcher at EPFL’s Laboratory of Intelligent Systems, where he focused on tensegrity robotics. His PhD research at the Czech Technical University focused on developing a robotic system combining reconfigurable and soft robotics for architectural and construction applications.
